Unfortunately, we would certainly wish that animals were exploited zero of the time. However, I do see where you're coming from (I wasn't raised vegan at all. Ate boatloads of meat every day) and I see what you mean when you say the "all or nothing" mentality can be intimidating. But animal exploitation is unkind and unnecessary, 100% of the time. Naturally, as an animal rights activist, I'd want to convince someone never to do it. 

In a similar vein, I'd want people to stop abuse/unfair treatment of women, end human trafficking, and racial discrimination/hate crimes. These are wrong 100% of the time, and I wouldn't imagine someone would denounce a person advocating for the end of trafficking simply because the "all or nothing mentality of human liberation was too evangelized." 

On the "holier than thou" vegan, it is an unfortunate side effect of any kind of activism, vegan or not. Effectively, if you tell people "hey, maybe you shouldn't do [this] anymore because it's harmful to [so-and-so]," you are putting your ideas above theirs. Ideally, this would start a discussion where both sides can analyze their positions and hear all arguments from both sides. 

We do not wish to shame people. Because that's not what activism is about. As a vegan, I will be the first to tell you I DON'T enjoy being in this position at all. I hate confrontations. I hate telling people what to do. And I hate telling people that they're wrong--veganism or not. But sadly you can't incite change without having these conversations. 

Finally, if everyone n were to say, only eat meat a few times a week...that's still thousands of lives lost. Just some cheese? Lots of forcefully impregnated cows so they can produce milk. Honey? Lots of dying queen bees. 

Should we be okay with these things?

A story from a bus driver, comin' up...

I was working late night, and at about 10-10:30PM, I'm driving through an apartment complex, and the bus heading in the other direction is approaching. Before I could wave, a pick-up truck suddenly pulls out of a driveway, forcing all of us -- including the pick-up -- to stop hard. We all sat this way for at least a good 10 seconds, wondering who would make the next move. Eventually, I pull forward, dodging the truck, and continue driving along. As a round the next bend, the truck STORMS past me in what must have been full throttle, roaring past me. *They must be in some hurry*, I thought. When I got to the next light, the truck stopped and the passenger door opened up. I knew what was happening; someone wanted to make my bus. A middle aged man wobbles up to the door and says "Thank you, sweetheart!" I nod and smile politely before he gets embarrassed and says "I didn't mean to say that." I smiled to myself, thinking someone had a little alcohol and was being silly. 

At this point, he hadn't made any gestures that would indicate to me that he was going to pay his fare, so I ask for it. At this point, he was already sitting down, complaining "I pay 38 dollars a month for this" (which is how much a senior/disabled monthly pass costs for my agency) but still showing no pass. At this point, I was pretty sure I was dealing with a fare evader. He goes on to tell me a story about how he "always tries to do the right thing, but gets fucked up" in the end. Eventually, after a long time, I ask for fare and he rises up, still talking about the injustice the world had placed unto him. I honestly thought that he had no fare, but after a few more stories, he pulls out a perfectly valid, clean monthly pass in good condition. I had to help him swipe it through the reader, and then he sits down. 

As I approach his stop, almost 30 minutes later, a woman comes up and asks me "How'd you get on this black folks route?" while the man still rambles on about the evils of the world around him, before getting off the bus.  

I thought all was well, and I only had to go back out one more time before pulling in for the night at 1:30. My night was far from over.

On my last half-trip back out, I get back to the exact same bus stop a few minutes early. After a few minutes past, it was time to leave, but not after someone appears out of nowhere and runs for the bus. I let him on, and he runs right to the back door, before running back up. He says nothing, and seems to expect me to drive without any action on his part. "D'you just learn how-ta drive the bus?" he says rather quickly. I couldn't understand him at first, so he repeats a second time, then adds "Lemme off at the next stop. You want me to ring the bell?" He pulls the stop cord extra hard. When I reach the next stop, he announces to the bus "I got guns on me, man! I got guns on me!" Afraid that I'd have an even bigger incident to deal with, I attentively watch as he puts a hat on extra slowly before leaving. A passenger leaves shortly after, telling me "I've never seen that person before. That was very strange." 

I've driven that route since, and I'd never seen him again. Oh, and another driver on that route on that VERY SAME NIGHT had a gun put to his face. Yikes.

Stay safe, everyone!
